title: National Parks, Sanctuaries, and Biosphere Reserves of India: Quiz

questions.question: Which was India's first national park, set up in 1936?
questions.rationale: Jim Corbett (originally Hailey National Park) in Uttarakhand was the first, in 1936. Kaziranga and Kanha came much later.

questions.question: The only natural home of the Asiatic lion is:
questions.rationale: Gir in Gujarat holds the Asiatic lion. Ranthambore and Sariska are tiger areas, and Dachigam is known for the hangul.

questions.question: Which national park is the world's only floating national park, home to the sangai deer?
questions.rationale: Keibul Lamjao sits on Loktak Lake in Manipur and floats on its phumdis (floating biomass). Bhitarkanika is a mangrove park in Odisha.

questions.question: Project Tiger was launched in which year?
questions.rationale: Project Tiger began in 1973. Project Elephant is the one launched in 1992, which is the usual trap.

questions.question: Which of these was NOT among the nine original Project Tiger reserves of 1973-74?
questions.rationale: The original nine were Bandipur, Corbett, Kanha, Manas, Melghat, Palamau, Ranthambore, Similipal and the Sunderbans. Kaziranga is known for rhinos and was not on that list.

questions.question: The hangul (Kashmir stag) is protected mainly in which national park?
questions.rationale: Dachigam, near Srinagar, is the hangul's home. Hemis in Ladakh is famous for the snow leopard and is the largest national park.

questions.question: Which was the first biosphere reserve notified in India, in 1986?
questions.rationale: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve (Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka) was the first, in 1986. The others were notified later.

questions.question: The Ramsar Convention on wetlands was signed in 1971 in which country?
questions.rationale: The treaty is named for the Iranian city of Ramsar. Do not pick Switzerland, which merely hosts the Ramsar secretariat.

questions.question: Which pair were India's first two Ramsar sites, designated on 1 October 1981?
questions.rationale: Chilika (Odisha) and Keoladeo (Rajasthan) were the first two. Loktak is on the Montreux Record, not a first-two site.

questions.question: Project Elephant was launched in:
questions.rationale: Project Elephant began in 1992. 1973 is Project Tiger, and 2010 is the year the elephant was declared the National Heritage Animal.

questions.question: Which statement about lakes is correct?
options: Chilika is the largest freshwater lake in India
Wular is the largest brackish-water lagoon
Chilika is the largest brackish-water lagoon and Wular the largest freshwater lake
Loktak is the largest brackish-water lagoon
questions.rationale: Chilika (Odisha) is the brackish lagoon, and Wular (Jammu and Kashmir) is the large freshwater lake. The wrong options swap or misassign them.

questions.question: Two Indian Ramsar sites on the Montreux Record (wetlands under threat) are:
questions.rationale: Keoladeo and Loktak are the two sites named in the lesson on the Montreux Record. Chilika was removed from it earlier after restoration.

questions.question: Which Act first created the legal framework for national parks and sanctuaries in India, and which amendment added community and conservation reserves?
questions.rationale: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 is the base law, and the 2002 amendment introduced conservation and community reserves.

questions.question: Eravikulam National Park in Kerala is best known for which species?
questions.rationale: Eravikulam protects the Nilgiri tahr. The lion-tailed macaque is the Silent Valley pairing, the red panda goes with Namdapha, and the bustard with Desert National Park.

questions.question: In 2022 cheetahs from Namibia were brought to which national park in Madhya Pradesh?
questions.rationale: Kuno National Park received the first cheetahs from Namibia in 2022 under the reintroduction programme.
